ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The large flag in the figure is an external large rectangle, with one vertical small rectangle on each of the left and right sides, and these two vertical small rectangles both extend from the top of the large rectangle to the bottom. The middle region is divided by two horizontal lines into three horizontally placed small rectangles, so there are altogether five congruent small rectangles. Reasoning: Let the short side of each small rectangle be s, and the long side be L. From the figure, it can be seen that the height of the vertical small rectangles on the left and right sides is just the height of the whole flag, therefore the height of the flag is L. The three congruent small rectangles in the middle are stacked up and down, and the height of each small rectangle in the vertical direction is the short side s, so the height of the whole flag is also 3s. Thus L=3s, so s/L=1/3. The problem asks that the side-length ratio of the small rectangle be written as lambda:1 and lambda<1, therefore lambda=1/3. Hence 360lambda=360*(1/3)=120.

method.method_draft: Assign variables to the congruent small rectangle: let its shorter side be s and longer side be L. From the image, the two outside rectangles are vertical and each spans the full height of the large flag, so the flag height is L. The middle region is made of three congruent rectangles stacked horizontally, so the same flag height is 3s. Equate L=3s, giving s/L=1/3. Since the requested ratio is lambda:1 with lambda<1, lambda=1/3, so 360lambda=120.
